extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, institutional compliance officers, higher-education counsel, and stakeholders commenting on Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble guidance and regulatory interpretations for implementing Title IX definitions and grievance-procedure obligations (e.g., what counts as a "complaint," scope of "sex-based harassment," disciplinary sanctions, burdens on recipients, and related procedural flexibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "complaint" — oral or written
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may be made orally or in writing; recipients may not deny a complaint simply because it was not submitted in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised definition provides added flexibility to the complaint process to avoid discouraging reports; recipients should not grant themselves discretion to deny complaints for lack of a written, signed document. Recipients already have obligations to evaluate conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (§106.31) and to offer supportive measures with or without a formal complaint (34 CFR 106.44(a)). Allowing oral complaints may increase reporting but the Department finds the benefits justify the possibility of increased complaints. Recipients are encouraged (but not required) to have employees other than the Title IX Coordinator keep notes or memorialize oral allegations; specific recordkeeping requirements for each complaint and each notification received are in §106.8(f). A recipient must initiate grievance procedures consistent with §106.45 only when a written or oral report meets the standards for a “complaint” in §106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR deference to recipient determinations (§106.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary (OCR) will not deem a recipient to have violated the regulations solely because OCR would have reached a different determination than the recipient did under §106.45 (i.e., OCR will not substitute its weighing of evidence for the recipient's decisionmaker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.47 conveys that OCR will not substitute its judgment for the recipient's decisionmaker regarding weighing of relevant evidence. However, §106.47 does not prevent OCR from holding a recipient accountable for noncompliance with any provision of the final regulations, including how the recipient determined whether a communication constitutes a complaint under §106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' duty to evaluate and address conduct that may constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is obligated to evaluate conduct that reasonably may constitute discrimination on the basis of sex and ensure redress where appropriate because recipients must operate education programs or activities free from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty exists independently of whether a formal, signed complaint is filed (see §106.31). Encouraging reporting and facilitating complaints is part of the recipient's obligation as a condition of receiving Federal funds. Recipients should balance investigation burdens against the mandate to provide equal educational opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for complaints and notifications (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations at §106.8(f) contain specific recordkeeping requirements for each complaint of sex discrimination and each notification the Title IX Coordinator receives of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While professors and other employees may find it helpful to document oral allegations, the Department declines to require employees to keep such records or mandate specific training on recordkeeping beyond §106.8(d). Recipients must follow the recordkeeping obligations spelled out in §106.8(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "disciplinary sanctions"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Disciplinary sanctions" are consequences imposed on a respondent only after a determination that the respondent has violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination (now clarified to be 'under Title IX').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition does not prescribe what consequences a recipient can or must impose nor what factors to consider when imposing sanctions; administrative enforcement does not override recipient discretion to make disciplinary decisions under their own policies and codes of conduct. The process for imposing disciplinary sanctions is detailed in §106.45(h). The regulations do not preclude routine classroom management or separate codes of conduct, including conduct determined not to be sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of educational institution categories (elementary/secondary/postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of 'elementary school,' 'secondary school,' and 'postsecondary institution' clarify Title IX coverage and apply to recipients; the postsecondary definition includes vocational institutions serving postsecondary students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations apply to all recipients of Federal financial assistance, including elementary and secondary schools, though some provisions (e.g., §106.46) explicitly only apply to postsecondary institutions. The Department streamlined the postsecondary definition and retained it to provide necessary clarification; commenters' concerns about micromanaging or creating an extrajudicial system were rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex-based harassment is a form of sex discrimination (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final definition explicitly states that 'sex-based harassment' is a form of sex discrimination and includes sexual harassment and harassment on the bases described in §106.10; conduct must be 'on the basis of sex.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition aligns with Title IX, precedent, and OCR experience. It covers discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity. The Department will consider differences in age/maturity across settings and allows recipients to adapt regulations appropriately. State workplace harassment laws may generally be applied where not in conflict with Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of sex-based harassment covered (quid pro quo, hostile environment, specific offenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: To constitute prohibited sex-based harassment, sexual harassment or other harassment on the bases described in §106.10 must satisfy one or more of three categories: quid pro quo, hostile environment, or listed specific offenses (e.g., sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department changed wording from 'other conduct' to 'other harassment' to tie it to §106.10 and clarified that the three categories modify both sexual harassment and other harassment on the basis of sex. Sexual harassment refers to conduct of a sexual nature and can include unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal, nonverbal, or physical conduct of a sexual nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered forms and settings of harassment (including online and nonsexual conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts of verbal, nonverbal, or physical aggression, intimidation, or hostility based on sex are within Title IX's purview and may constitute sex-based harassment if they meet the definition; such conduct can occur online as well as in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department affirms that 'on the basis of sex' does not require the conduct be sexual in nature; harassment based on pregnancy, gender identity, or sex stereotypes is included. Online harassment is explicitly within scope and recipients should address harassment irrespective of medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient accountability for responding to all forms of sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations hold a recipient accountable for responding to sex-based harassment, including quid pro quo harassment, hostile environment harassment, sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking, consistent with Title IX's broad prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respond across all populations, acknowledging that individuals may experience intersecting forms of discrimination. Implementing Title IX does not displace other civil-rights obligations enforced by OCR or other agencies; an improved Title IX response benefits those with overlapping discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected burden and cost considerations; Department's justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department projected a 10 percent increase in complaint investigations compared to the 2020 amendments and determined the related costs are justified by benefits of ensuring effective implementation of Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered alternatives and addressed small-entity impacts in the Regulatory Flexibility Act discussion, projecting a similar 10 percent increase for small recipients. Commenters provided no data to warrant changing that estimate. Recipients are afforded regulatory flexibilities (e.g., discretion to use a single-investigator model, removal of mandatory live hearing in all cases (§§106.45(b)(2), 106.46(f)(1))) to mitigate burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Title IX Coordinator obligations and First Amendment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinator requirements do not impose an obligation to monitor or limit conduct or speech beyond conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; nothing in the regulations requires restricting constitutional rights such as the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that the regulations require Title IX Coordinators to police potentially offensive but constitutionally protected speech. §106.6(d) remains in force: nothing requires a recipient to restrict rights protected by the U.S. Constitution. The Department will consider First Amendment issues separately (see Hostile Environment—First Amendment Considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation for age, maturity, and educational setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations take into account differences in age and maturity of students in various educational settings, allowing recipients to adapt the regulations as appropriate to fulfill Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying the definition of sex-based harassment and responding to complaints, recipients should consider contextual differences (e.g., elementary vs. postsecondary) on a case-by-case basis while still complying with Title IX and the final regulations.
